while Statement

　The while statement repeatedly executes a statement or block while a specified condition is true. It allows you to create loops.
　The syntax is as follows:

while(expression)
    statement or block

　The "statement or block" is executed repeatedly as long as the conditional expression `expression` is true.

　The behavior is as follows:
(1) First, `expression` is evaluated; if it is false, the statement or block is not executed.
(2) Execute the statement or block.
(3) Evaluate `expression`; if the result is true, go to (2), otherwise the `while` statement ends.

　In other words, if `expression` is false from the beginning, the statement or block will not be executed. Also, `expression` is not continuously evaluated; its truth value is checked once after each execution of the statement or block.
　In addition, at step (3), in the case of a block, execution temporarily leaves the block (meaning variables inside are destroyed).

Example:
    while(func()) ;
    /* While func() is true, do nothing and keep evaluating func() */

    while(func()) i++;
    /* While func() is true, keep executing i++ */

    while(i < 5) // While i is less than 5
    {
        func(i);
        i++;
    }

break

　The `break` statement is used when you want to terminate the `while` loop prematurely.

Example:
    while(true) // Infinite loop unless break is executed
    {
        if(func()) break; // If func() is true, end while
        func2(); // Reaches here if break above is not executed
    }
    // Reaches here when break is executed

continue

　The `continue` statement is used when you want to skip the rest of the loop and restart from evaluating the conditional expression.
　When `continue` is executed, control transfers to (3).

Example:
    var i = 0;
    while(i < 5)
    {
        if(func1()) continue;
        // If func1() is true, the condition check i < 5 is performed, and if true,
        // execution starts again from the beginning of the block
        func2();
        i++;
    }

do...while

　The `do...while` statement is the same as the `while` statement, but it does not check the conditional expression at the beginning.
　The syntax is as follows:

do
    statement or block
while(expression);

　Because the condition is not checked first, even if the conditional expression is false at the `do` point, the "statement or block" will still be executed once.
　Once the "statement or block" is executed, the conditional expression is checked; if false, it exits the loop, and if true, the statement or block is executed again, repeating this process.
